clinician.final_diagnosis: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome Associated with Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 8-year-old boy presented with a 3-day history of fever, progressive left ear pain and swelling, and a vesicular rash around the left ear pinna. On day 2 of admission, he developed lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy, dizziness, and increased sleepiness. On day 3, he further developed vomiting, dysarthria, and unsteady gait. VZV PCR from an ear swab was positive, while bacterial culture and HSV PCR were negative. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed 10 leukocytes (8 mononuclear, 2 polymorphonuclear) and 2 red cells with normal protein and glucose, and VZV PCR from CSF was positive. An urgent brain MRI and MRV were reported as normal. Following these findings, intravenous acyclovir and oral prednisolone were initiated.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with fever, left ear pain/swelling, and vesicular rash around the left ear pinna, suggestive of VZV reactivation.
Development of lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy, a key feature of Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.
Development of neurological symptoms including dizziness, sleepiness, vomiting, dysarthria, and unsteady gait, indicating central nervous system involvement.
Confirmation of Varicella-Zoster Virus infection by positive VZV PCR from the ear swab.
Evidence of encephalitis with positive VZV PCR from cerebrospinal fluid.
Cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis (10 leukocytes) consistent with encephalitis.
Initiation of antiviral (acyclovir) and corticosteroid (prednisolone) treatment for VZV encephalitis.
